title: NAT Gateway Bytes Processed and Connection Tracking

detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=aws`.
• Install and configure `Splunk_TA_aws` with the modular input for `aws:cloudwatch`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.1.78.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `metric_name` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Collect NAT Gateway metrics. Alert on sudden drop in BytesOutToDestination (possible outage) or spike in ActiveConnectionCount (possible connection exhaustion). Track data processed for cost.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudwatch" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudwatch" namespace="AWS/NATGateway"
| table _time metric_name namespace unit average maximum
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.1.32_nat_gateway_bytes_proces_32"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `aws:cloudwatch` in `index=aws` to detect nat gateway bytes processed and connection tracking. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the Amazon CloudWatch console Metrics for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `metric_name` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_1_32_alert` with severity aligned to `medium` criticality. Dashboard: Line chart (bytes, connections by NAT GW), Table (NAT GW, bytes today), Single value..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade `Splunk_TA_aws` and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of nat gateway bytes processed and connection tracking so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
